conviction_note: The release carries one new line, the capital-return decision. Lancashire declared a special dividend at each of the last three Q3 statements (+8.2%, +6.5%, +4.0% on the day) and Q3 2026 nat-cat was benign. Two sourced negatives the market can largely compute work against it: a steep Q3 rise in Treasury yields on a 2.1-year-duration book, and Q3 large-risk losses that peers booked (Barzan/Ras Laffan at full limit, more Middle East war, Ukraine aviation). The findings net to about +0.1. The stock also ran 9% in 20 days to a 52-week high above the 664p consensus target, so much of the dividend is plausibly priced. That leaves p_up at 55 on a 5.5% scale, +0.55. The two numbers agree in sign and both are small because the decisive number, the size of the special, is unknown.

findings.finding: A Q3 special dividend is the scheduled capital-return event. Lancashire declared one at each of the last three Q3 statements: Nov 2023 $119m special plus up to $50m buyback, Nov 2024 75c/$180m, Nov 2025 75c/$182m. Q3 2026 nat-cat was benign ($29bn industry, 31% below average, little hurricane), so a fourth is likely.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q3 statement days: 2022-11-03 +5.7%, 2023-11-09 +8.2%, 2024-11-06 +6.5%, 2025-11-05 +4.0%. All four up, with the reaction shrinking as the special became expected. Non-Q3 results were sold: FY25 -2.9%, H1 26 -6.6%
findings.original_quote: the Board has approved a special dividend of 75 cents per common share, resulting in an aggregate distribution of approximately $182 million
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced. The stock is +9.0% in 20 days and +16.8% in 60 to 693p, above the 664p average target and at a 52-week high, which is what anticipation of a special looks like. What is not priced is the SIZE: no published consensus for it was found, and the April 2026 50c special plus Q3 mark-to-market losses make a repeat of 75c uncertain. If the full 75c were priced, the run-up would carry no residual and the stock would be sold on an in-line special, which is the left tail of this range.
findings.independence: Benign Q3 cat from a separate source: Aon via Artemis 2026-10-29 https://www.artemis.bm/news/global-insured-natural-catastrophe-losses-reach-91bn-in-9m26-lowest-since-2019-aon/ . Q3 2024 and Q3 2023 specials: https://www.investegate.co.uk/announcement/prn/lancashire-holdings-limited--lre/q3-trading-statement/8532293 and https://www.investegate.co.uk/announcement/prn/lancashire-holdings-limited--lre/q3-trading-statement/7869966

findings.finding: US yields rose sharply in Q3 2026: 2y 4.14% to 4.88%, 5y 4.19% to 5.09%, with a Fed hike on 16 Sep. On Lancashire's disclosed 2.1-year duration and ~$2.97bn of fixed maturities and cash, that is roughly a -$50m mark-to-market against ~$38m of quarterly income. Q3 total investment return is likely flat to negative, and 9M below 1% against 5.6% a year earlier.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: H1 2026: total investment return fell to $51.3m from $108.2m on a -$29.6m mark-to-market. That was part of the profit miss, and the stock fell 6.6%
findings.why_not_priced: Yields are public and analysts model duration, so most of this is computable. The H1 profit miss against consensus, partly on mark-to-market, shows the street can still under-model this line. If it were fully priced, the stock would not have rallied 17% over a quarter in which the book lost value.
findings.independence: Duration and book yield from Lancashire's own H1 release https://www.investegate.co.uk/announcement/prn/lancashire-holdings-limited--lre/lancashire-holdings-h1-2026-results/9692595 ; peer Hamilton took a $56m Q3 fixed-income trading loss on rising rates https://www.investing.com/news/transcripts/earnings-call-transcript-hamilton-insurance-group-posts-strong-q3-2026-operating-profit-93CH-4989592 ; RenRe $899.6m fixed-maturity losses 'primarily due to increases in market yields' https://www.reinsurancene.ws/renre-trims-property-book-as-underwriting-result-offsets-losses-in-casualty-and-specialty-segment/

findings.finding: Peers booked Q3 large-risk losses in exactly Lancashire's core specialty lines. RenRe reserved its share of a $1.7bn full-limit Barzan/Ras Laffan energy loss (>$59m) and almost $70m of Middle East war losses. Hamilton booked $17m of Ras Laffan and $42m of Ukraine-related specialty/aviation reserve strengthening. Lancashire is a leading London energy, war/political-violence and aviation writer, and its Q3 loss commentary may name these.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q3 2024: named Helene/Debby/Milton losses and guided the undiscounted combined ratio to the high end of range; the stock still rose 6.5% on the special. Q3 2025's 'active' large-risk commentary was absorbed (+4.0%). Large-risk commentary has not driven a Q3 day before
findings.why_not_priced: Lancashire has disclosed nothing on Barzan; the event was 21 June, and H1 said no large loss was individually material. Peers booked it in Q3 on a reporting lag, so Lancashire may well have too. The market has the peer numbers but not Lancashire's share. Since peers reported (28 Oct) the stock rose from 677p to 693p, so the market is not discounting a material hit.
